Connolly is the filer of H.810, a bill to extend voting rights in municipal elections to noncitizen residents. Page text: 'By Representative Connolly of Cambridge, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 810) of Mike Connolly relative to extending voting rights in municipal elections to noncitizen voters.'

findings.passage: That proposal was opposed by the Speaker and did not pass, but I have continued co-sponsoring Same-Day Registration bills because voting should be made more accessible — not more difficult.
findings.note: Campaign site statement on voting access, about same-day registration. It does not name ID or citizenship documents. Saved as related material only.

findings.passage: In 2022, I was one of 61 House Democrats who voted to advance Same-Day Voter Registration, allowing eligible residents to register and vote on Election Day. That proposal was opposed by the Speaker and did not pass, but I have continued co-sponsoring Same-Day Registration bills because voting should be made more accessible — not more difficult. This fall, Same-Day Voter Registration will be a ballot question, and I am campaigning for a Yes vote.
findings.note: Campaign site text, undated, written before the 2026 primary. Related to registration rules, not to ID or citizenship proof. He says he backs same-day registration and says voting should be made more accessible, not more difficult. Same-day registration is a related topic; the page says nothing on photo ID or citizenship documents.

Progressive Massachusetts scorecard lists him among the House sponsors of H.834 (companion S.505), 'An Act establishing same day registration of voters'. The scorecard describes it as enabling eligible citizens to register to vote at the polls. The official malegislature.gov page was blocked, so the exact co-sponsor date and the bill's proof-of-residence text were not read. Related topic: registration process.
